ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription

acceptedAnswer.text: A MET (metabolic equivalent of task) compares an activity's energy use with sitting at rest. 1 MET is resting; running at 6 mph is 9.3 METs, meaning it uses roughly 9.3 times as much energy per minute.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between gross and net calories burned?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gross calories include what your body would have burned at rest during that time. Net calories subtract that resting amount, which is a fairer figure when deciding how much extra energy exercise used.

mainEntity.name: Why is my fitness tracker's number different?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trackers combine heart rate, movement and their own algorithms, while this calculator uses average MET values for each activity. Both are estimates — use one method consistently to track changes over time.

mainEntity.name: How many calories does walking a mile burn?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 100 gross calories for a 75 kg (165 lb) person at roughly 3 mph, and about 108 at 3.5 to 4 mph. Net of resting calories it is about 73 to 89. Heavier people burn more per mile.

mainEntity.name: How many calories do 10,000 steps burn?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 75 kg person with a 0.75 m stride at about 3 mph, 10,000 steps takes around 1.55 hours and burns roughly 465 gross calories (about 343 net). Lighter people and shorter strides burn less.

mainEntity.name: How many calories does a 30-minute run burn?

acceptedAnswer.text: At 6 mph (MET 9.3) a 60 kg person burns about 293 calories in 30 minutes, a 75 kg person about 366 and a 90 kg person about 439.

mainEntity.name: How many calories do I burn in an hour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply the per-minute figure by 60. A 75 kg person burns about 299 an hour walking at 3 mph, about 630 an hour cycling at 12–13.9 mph, and about 732 an hour running at 6 mph.

mainEntity.name: Does body weight change how many calories I burn?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The formula multiplies by weight, so a 90 kg person burns 50% more than a 60 kg person doing the same activity for the same time.

mainEntity.name: Should I eat back the calories I burn exercising?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. The estimates are averages and wearables can be off by 10–20%. If your calorie target already includes your activity level, eating back workout calories counts them twice.

mainEntity.name: Why does another calories burned calculator give a different answer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Calculators use different MET tables and formulas. This one uses MET × 3.5 × kg ÷ 200 per minute. Calculators that use 1 kcal per kg per hour for each MET show about 5% less.

mainEntity.name: Is this calculator suitable for steps or walking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, choose a walking activity and enter your time. To convert steps to time, divide the steps by your steps per minute, which depends on stride length and pace.
